report:
## Conclusion

The claim is **partially supported but overstated** — evidence suggests vegetarian diets are associated with modestly lower mortality risk in some populations, but this is not a proven, universal causal effect, and results are inconsistent across studies.

**What the evidence shows:**

- The largest, most-cited cohort — the **Adventist Health Study-2** (73,308 Seventh-day Adventists) — found vegetarian diets associated with lower all-cause mortality, with effects more robust in men, and later follow-up confirmed reduced cause-specific mortality among vegetarians (https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamainternalmedicine/fullarticle/1710093; https://ajcn.nutrition.org/article/S0002-9165(24)00652-X/fulltext). However, Adventists as a group avoid smoking/alcohol and are health-conscious, making it hard to isolate diet's independent effect.

- A large Australian cohort (267,180 people) found only modest associations with all-cause mortality after adjustment (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0091743516304479).

- A 2021 meta-analysis found vegetarian diets reduced **ischemic heart disease mortality** but had **no significant effect on all-cause or cerebrovascular mortality**, and rated the evidence "low certainty" (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34611632/).

- Broader reviews of "plant-based diet indices" (which include more than strict vegetarianism) show more consistent associations with reduced all-cause, cancer, and cardiovascular mortality (https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/nutrition/articles/10.3389/fnut.2024.1481363/full), suggesting diet *quality* (whole plant foods vs. processed) matters more than simply excluding meat.

**Bottom line:** Vegetarian/plant-based dietary patterns are linked to lower cardiovascular mortality and possibly modest reductions in all-cause mortality, but the effect on overall life expectancy is smaller and less certain than popular claims suggest, and confounding by lifestyle factors remains a significant limitation across the observational evidence.
